steps.body: Let $\alpha \in A$ be independent of $A\setminus\{\alpha\}$. Then $A' = A\setminus\{\alpha\}$ proves neither $\alpha$ (independence) nor $\neg\alpha$ ($A'$ is consistent with $\alpha$, since $A$ is consistent). So $A'$ is incomplete. Example: the empty subsystem of a complete theory proves only tautologies.
